before.content:
<!-- layout: title; theme: keynote; design: v1 -->
# The intake pilot

A shorter review cycle, with an unanswered quality question. [1][2]

---

<!-- layout: composed -->
<!-- scene:  -->
## The pilot measured time; quality remains unknown [1][2]

In this synthetic intake pilot, median review time was 40 hours before the pilot and 16 hours during the pilot. The observation covered two teams over eight weeks. These are training data, not actual organizational results. [1]

The two-team intake pilot did not measure review quality or error rates. A faster review cannot establish a quality improvement. The sample does not establish an effect in other teams. [2]

beforeFindings.problem: Body text is 17.8px; the body floor is 22px.
beforeFindings.correction: Allocate more room and increase type; keep values and qualifications intact.

beforeFindings.problem: The limitation copy in b2 renders at 17.75 px, under the 22 px body minimum, and it is the slide's essential qualification (quality and error rates were not measured). The same slide sets the time narration at 22.72 px, so the caveat is visually weaker than the result it constrains.
beforeFindings.correction: Set b2 body type back to at least 22 px and give it a measure wide enough to hold it at that size (the block already reserves 816 px of width, so only the type size needs raising). Keep every word and the trailing [2] marker intact.

beforeFindings.problem: The left column is only 204 px wide, so the time result breaks into about 15 lines of three to four words each while the right column's two lines sit at the top with roughly 450 px of empty space beneath them; fit is 0.71 and the lower-right half of the stage is dead.
beforeFindings.correction: Rebalance the two columns in the scene/layout metadata: widen b1 to a readable measure (roughly 380-420 px) and start b2 lower or let it fill the freed width, so the composition uses the full stage height without changing any wording.

beforeFindings.problem: The headline result (median 40 hours before the pilot, 16 hours during) is buried in running prose at the same weight as the observational caveats, so the number the audience is deciding on does not read as the key fact.
beforeFindings.correction: Within the existing text, keep the wording but give the two figures stronger display treatment in the layout (larger size or a distinct emphasis run for the 40 hours / 16 hours phrases) so the result leads and the qualifications still follow clearly.
